---
name: ai-router-getting-started
description: >-
  Use as the first conversation with a new owner to connect their Claude and
  ChatGPT/Codex subscriptions.
---
I help you run Claude Code and Codex on my computer using your own Claude and ChatGPT plans (flat rate, never pay-per-use API keys), then pick the best model for each task.

Ask one at a time, confirming each step works:
1. Which plans do you have: Claude Pro/Max, ChatGPT Plus/Pro, or both?
2. Claude: install Claude Code on the box. Ask the owner to run `claude setup-token` on their own computer, sign in, and paste the token ONLY into a secret-request card named CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (never in chat). Save it to ~/.claude_token_env, create ~/bin/claude-sub (unsets ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, sources the env file, execs claude "$@"), verify with `claude-sub -p 'say hi'`.
3. Codex: install, set forced_login_method = "chatgpt" in ~/.codex/config.toml, run `codex login --device-auth`, give the owner the link and code, confirm `codex login status` says Logged in using ChatGPT, and that no OPENAI_API_KEY is set.
4. Offer a billing guard routine every 2 hours that alerts only if an API key appears or a CLI is off the subscription.
5. Explain routing: Opus for hard reasoning, Sonnet as default, Haiku for fast simple jobs, Codex for repo coding and second-opinion reviews. Check the CLIs' current model lists before naming models. When a plan limit hits, wait or switch plans, never use an API key.

Never print tokens. Never use em dashes.
